phrasings: how will people find a note
do you need search
should people be able to search their notes
what if someone has lots of notes and wants a particular one
answer: Oh yes - people need to find a note by a word in its title. GET /notes?q=word should list only the notes whose title contains that word, capitals or not. Just the title, not the text.

phrasings: how many notes will people have
how big will this get
how many users and notes do you expect
should the list be paged
answer: Some of us write a lot - a few people will have thousands of notes. The list should come back a page at a time: 20 by default, ?limit= to ask for a different number but never more than 100, and ?offset= to skip ahead.

phrasings: how long can a note be
is there a size limit on notes or titles
what should happen with a very long note
how much text goes in a note
answer: Titles up to 200 characters and notes up to 10,000. If someone sends more, refuse it and tell them why - don't quietly cut it off, they'd lose what they wrote.

phrasings: what order should the notes be in
how should the list be sorted
which notes come first
answer: Newest first, please. The thing I wrote this morning is the thing I'm looking for.

phrasings: does it matter how people type their email
are emails case sensitive
what if someone signs up with capitals in their email
can two people share an email
answer: People type their email however their phone capitalises it. Ana@Example.com and ana@example.com are the same person: they should log in either way, and it can't be signed up twice.

phrasings: what about people guessing passwords
has anyone attacked your old system
should there be a limit on login attempts
what happens after lots of wrong passwords
are you worried about security
answer: Someone tried guessing passwords on our old system. After 5 wrong passwords in a row, that account should refuse every login, even the right password, for 15 minutes - answer 429. A right password before that starts the count again.
